---
title: "Start bridge (@tuturuuu/start-bridge)"
description: "The frozen v0 contract for running Next App Router satellites on TanStack Start + Vite+ on Cloudflare, including the basePath and per-app session cookie rules."
---

`@tuturuuu/start-bridge` is the shared layer that lets a satellite's existing
App Router source run under TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void on a Cloudflare
Worker. It replaces the per-app `src/runtime` shim copies in Meet, Mail and
Calendar. The core (`route-match`, `base-path`, `mounts`, `app-url`, `endpoints`,
`pages`, `api-forward`, `canary`, `request-context`) has no React, Start or
Vite imports; the `next/*`, `start/*`, `intl/*` and `vite` entries are the
framework adapters at the edge.

This page is the **v0 API freeze**. App lanes convert against these export
paths and signatures. Within v0, changes are additive only: a new optional
option, a new export, or a new subpath. Removing or changing a frozen
signature needs a new subpath and a coordinated migration.

## Worker handler

```ts
import { createFunctionProxy } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/function-proxy';
import { createBridgeHandler } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/handler';
import { createBridgeStartHandler } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/server-entry';
import { proxy } from '../src/proxy';
import { endpoints } from '../src/runtime/api-registry.bridge.gen';

export default {
  fetch: createBridgeHandler<Env, ExecutionContext>({
    mounts: {
      app: 'meet',
      rootHosts: ['meet.tuturuuu.com'],
      mountHosts: ['tuturuuu.com'],
      basePath: '/meet',
    },
    start: createBridgeStartHandler(),
    serverFnBase: '/_serverFn',
    proxy,
    endpoints,
    functionBase: '/_serverFn',
    functionProxy: createFunctionProxy({ targetApp: 'meet' }),
    publicAssets,
    assets: (env) => env.ASSETS,
    centralApiOrigin: (env) => env.INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN ?? 'https://tuturuuu.com',
  }),
};
```

Order: base resolution from `mounts` (a mount host outside the mount is 404),
`/assets/*` and declared public files from `ASSETS` (base-stripped), then the
app's `proxy.ts`, `centralFirst` paths to the central API (Next `beforeFiles`
rewrites such as `TUTURUUU_WEB_WORKSPACE_API_RESERVED_PATHS`; Next sources
like `/api/v1/:wsId/x` or bracket patterns), the generated endpoint registry,
unowned `/api/*` to the central API (base-stripped), server functions to Start (base-stripped), and
finally pages to Start at the browser-visible URL. The response then gets
Location rewriting. Cookies pass through unchanged. A `proxy.ts` rewrite to
another origin throws unless that origin is the configured central API origin
(`rewriteOrigins`), which is then fetched with manual redirects and hop-by-hop
headers removed.

In the app: `start.ts` passes `serverFns: { fetch: bridgeServerFnFetch }` to
`createStart`, `getRouter()` sets `basepath: routerBasepath()`, and the root
route lists `appBaseHeadScript()` first in `head().scripts`.

## Registries and the unregistered-route check

Each app declares `start-bridge.routes.json` at its root:

```json
{
  "appDir": "src/app",
  "stripSegments": { "[locale]": { "locale": "en" } },
  "api": { "out": "src/runtime/api-registry.bridge.gen.ts" },
  "pages": { "out": "src/runtime/page-registry.bridge.gen.ts" },
  "owned": { "api/build-info/route.ts": "src/native/api.server.ts" },
  "ignored": { "api/legacy/route.ts": "served by the central API" }
}
```

`bun packages/start-bridge/src/codegen/cli.ts generate apps/<app>` writes the
registries; `check` fails when a generated file is stale, a `route.*` or
`page.*` is neither generated, `owned` by an existing native file, nor
`ignored` with a reason, an `owned`/`ignored` entry names no file, two files
map to one pattern, or a parallel/intercepting route appears. Route groups are
dropped from patterns. The page manifest exports `PagePattern`; type the page
model as `satisfies Record<PagePattern, Loader>` so a new page fails
type-check until it is handled. `*.bridge.gen.ts` files are excluded from
Biome.

## basePath contract

One compiled artifact serves an app at its subdomain root and mounted at
`tuturuuu.com/<app>`. The Worker resolves the base **per request** from the
host and path against `mounts` (`rootHosts` → `''`; `mountHosts` + the
`/<app>` prefix → `/<app>`; unlisted hosts default to the root, or 404 with
`unknownHost: 'reject'`). The build-time `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH` is only the
fallback when no runtime base exists. Root mode is the identity everywhere.

| Concern | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Ownership | A mount host owns `/<app>` and `/<app>/*` only; `/meetings` is not `/meet` |
| SSR | The request context carries `appBase`; `runtimeAppBase()` reads it per request |
| Hydration | `appBaseHeadScript()` serializes the base before the client router starts |
| Router | `basepath: routerBasepath()` (`/` or `/<app>`) |
| Assets | The SSR manifest's script/stylesheet URLs get the request's base (`createBridgeStartHandler`); JS-referenced asset URLs read the runtime base (`renderBuiltUrl`), CSS ones stay relative to their stylesheet; requests are fetched from `ASSETS` base-stripped |
| Server functions | Compiled against the root (`/_serverFn`); `bridgeServerFnFetch` sends them to `/<app>/_serverFn` in the browser, and the Worker strips the base before Start |
| Next middleware | `NextRequest` carries Next's `basePath`; `nextUrl.pathname` is app-relative and `nextUrl.clone()` redirects keep the base |
| Links and navigation | `next/link`, `useRouter().push/replace`, `redirect()` prefix path-absolute hrefs with the runtime base |
| URLs in app code | `appPath('/...')` and `appUrl('/share/...', origin?)` from `app-url` (worklets, Live, preview, download, share) |
| Browser `/api` calls | Web-owned `/api` stays relative: on the apex it reaches Web directly, on a subdomain the Worker forwards it. App-owned endpoints must use `createApiPath(appApiPatterns, centralFirst)` (codegen `api.patternsOut` emits `appApiPatterns` without importing route modules); `@tuturuuu/internal-api` keeps calling Web relatively |
| Location headers | Path-relative `Location` not already under the base gains it. Absolute URLs are never rewritten, so `new URL('/login', request.url)` behaves as in Next (it leaves the app) |
| Central API | Unowned `/<app>/api/*` is forwarded as `/api/*` |
| Auth return URLs | `appUrl(path, origin)` so the central login returns into the app |
| Cookies | Never renamed or path-scoped. The canonical session cookie is `tuturuuu_app_session` (+ `tuturuuu_app_session_refresh`) everywhere; there is no per-app name. Subdomains keep today's behaviour until cutover; the apex uses the shared session below |

`tuturuuu.com/meet` is the Meet app root; product marketing moves to
`/products/<app>`.

## Shared session on the apex (proposal for security review)

**Decision (user, 2026-10-25):** keep one Tuturuuu session, usable across
every app; no per-app session cookies. The bridge therefore leaves all cookies
untouched. Making that safe on the apex needs the auth change below. It is a
**proposal awaiting security review**; nothing here is implemented yet.

### Current model and the apex problems

- Each satellite holds a per-app access token in `tuturuuu_app_session`
  (`target_app` = that app; `verifyAppSessionToken` requires an exact match)
  plus `tuturuuu_app_session_refresh`, host-only at `Path=/` on its subdomain.
- With `sessionMode: 'supabase-first'` and the root Supabase cookies
  (`sb-<ref>-auth-token*`, shared on `.tuturuuu.com`) present,
  `refreshAppSessionForRequest` already derives the app claims from Supabase,
  mints the access token **in memory** as `Authorization: Bearer` for that
  request, and then calls `clearAppSessionCookie`.
- On the apex, `clearAppSessionCookie` would expire `tuturuuu_app_session`,
  its refresh cookie **and Web's own `tuturuuu_web_app_session` (+ refresh)**
  at `Path=/` on every mounted-app request.
- Web's `createClient` (`packages/supabase/src/next/server.ts` and
  `request/server.ts`, `requestHasAppSessionAuth`) switches to the isolated
  app-session client whenever a `tuturuuu_app_session` cookie is present, so
  any app writing that cookie at `Path=/` on the apex drops Web's Supabase
  session. If several apps wrote it, they would overwrite each other's
  per-app token.

### Proposed model

1. **The shared apex session is the root Supabase session.** Its cookies
   already cover `.tuturuuu.com` with `Path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and
   `SameSite=Lax`, and every app already accepts it through `supabase-first`.
   Mounted apps derive their per-app claims per request (in-memory bearer, as
   today) and **never write or clear `tuturuuu_app_session*` or
   `tuturuuu_web_app_session*` on the apex**. No new token audience is
   needed: the audience check stays per app, and the Supabase JWT is
   validated on every request.
2. **Mounted mode is set by the bridge, not the client.** The handler deletes
   any incoming `x-tuturuuu-app-base` header and sets its own from the resolved
   mount. Auth treats a non-empty value as mounted mode.
3. **Subdomains keep today's behaviour** until each app's cutover.

### Code that must change (auth owner)

| Where | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/auth/src/proxy/index.ts` `refreshAppSessionForRequest` | Mounted mode: Supabase-only. Skip `resolveSignedAppSessionForRequest` (no `/api/auth/refresh-app-session` minting); a missing or invalid Supabase session goes to Web login with `appUrl(...)` as the return URL |
| same file, `createSupabaseBackedAppSessionResponse` | Mounted mode: keep the in-memory bearer and the Supabase `Set-Cookie` pass-through, but do **not** call `clearAppSessionCookie` |
| same file, `appSessionFailureResponse` | Mounted mode: no app-cookie clearing; MFA/failure redirects use absolute Web URLs |
| `packages/auth/src/app-session.ts` `clearAppSessionCookie` callers: each satellite's `app/api/auth/logout`, `refresh-app-session` and `verify-app-token` routes | Mounted mode: logout goes to Web sign-out (clears the shared Supabase session for every app); the refresh and verify routes are not used on the apex |
| `packages/supabase/src/next/server.ts`, `packages/supabase/src/request/server.ts` `requestHasAppSessionAuth` | Defence in depth: on the apex host, a valid Supabase cookie session wins over a cookie-borne `tuturuuu_app_session` (bearer app tokens unchanged), so a stale or foreign app cookie cannot drop Web's session |
| `@tuturuuu/start-bridge` `function-proxy` and the app `proxy.ts` calls | Pass mounted mode through to `refreshAppSessionForRequest` |
| `@tuturuuu/satellite/auth` `getSatelliteAppSessionUser` | No change expected: it reads the forwarded bearer; verify under mounted mode |

### Risks to review

- **Concurrent refresh-token rotation.** Web and several mounted apps may call
  `updateSession` at once and rotate the same Supabase refresh token. The
  Supabase reuse interval tolerates near-simultaneous reuse; verify the
  project setting before cutover.
- **Logout is global** on the apex by design: signing out of one app signs out
  of all of them.
- **Per-request cost.** Each mounted-app request validates the Supabase JWT
  instead of an HMAC app token. This is local with asymmetric signing keys;
  measure it in staging.
- **Subdomain → apex.** The Supabase session already covers both hosts, so a
  user with a valid root session needs no re-login. Users with only a satellite
  app session re-login once at cutover (user decision; no cross-host handoff).

## Page adapter (React Server Components)

`@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/page-route` renders App Router pages for Start
with React Server Components. `renderAppRouterPage({ page, layouts, params,
searchParams, render })` loads the page and its layouts, resolves metadata
root-down (layout title templates apply; `metadata` or `generateMetadata`),
awaits the page body and each layout so `notFound()`/`redirect()` reach the
router as a 404 or redirect, and returns `{ head, node }`. Call it from an
app-owned `createServerFn` handler with `render: renderServerComponent` from
`@tanstack/react-start/rsc`; the route loader returns it, `head()` spreads
`loaderData.head`, and the component renders `loaderData.node`.

Enable it with `startBridgePreset({ rsc: true })` (Start `rsc: { enabled }`)
and `rsc()` from `@vitejs/plugin-rsc` in the app's Vite plugins. The bridge
request store is anchored on `globalThis`, so `next/headers`, cookies and the
app base resolve inside the separately bundled `rsc` environment too.

Spike evidence (2026-10-26, a contacts-shaped fixture built by `vp build`
with Void and run from the emitted Worker in workerd): an async page with a
server-only read and `generateMetadata` rendered with the right `<title>`; a
`'use client'` child hydrated and handled clicks with no console errors;
`notFound()` answered 404 and `redirect()` 307; the server-only module and
its secret appeared in neither the client bundle nor the HTML; per-request
context reached the RSC bundle for distinct actors. Start's RSC support is
experimental (`@tanstack/react-start-rsc` 0.1.x): pin versions, keep
`'use client'` boundaries as in Next, and expect nested async components that
throw `notFound()` mid-stream to hit the error boundary rather than a 404.

## Canary mode (v0.2 interface)

`decideCohort({ percent, cookie, force, draw })` returns
`{ cohort: 'native' | 'legacy', reason, persist, percent }`. The share comes
from `TUTURUUU_NATIVE_CANARY_PERCENT` (`0`–`100`; invalid or missing is `0`,
which is `legacy`). A valid sticky cookie `tuturuuu_runtime_cohort` keeps its
cohort while the canary is on; new browsers are drawn against the share.
`tagResponse` sets `x-tuturuuu-runtime`, appends `Vary: Cookie`, and persists
only new draws, scoped to the app path. Production publication stays held per
`tuturuuu.ci.ts`; the router that uses these is v0.2 work.

## Vite preset

```ts
const bridge = startBridgePreset({
  appRoot: import.meta.url,
  app: 'apps',
  navigation: 'document',
  shims: ['next/headers', 'next/server', 'next/navigation', 'next/link', 'next-intl'],
  serverOnlySpecifiers: ['@tuturuuu/satellite/auth'],
});
export default defineConfig(({ command }) => ({
  base: bridge.base,
  define: bridge.define,
  plugins: [voidPlugin(), tanstackStart(bridge.tanstackStart), react(), tailwindcss()],
  environments: { client: { define: bridge.clientDefine(command) } },
  resolve: { alias: bridge.alias },
}));
```

`basePath` defaults to `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH` at build time. List `shims`
explicitly when converting an app whose current config aliases only some
`next/*` modules, so the bundle does not change.

## Verification

`packages/start-bridge` unit tests cover each core module and adapter at the
root and under `/meet`, plus the ported Meet proxy-bridge regressions. App
adoption still needs that app's exact-commit CI: unit, type-check, lint,
`vp build`, the sealed artifact and emitted-runtime acceptance where the app
has them.
